text: The defendant rents a storage unit in a commercial warehouse. Last year the defendant had a heated dispute with the warehouse owner over unpaid fees. One night in March, a fire started in the defendant's unit. The defendant set the fire deliberately, intending to destroy the warehouse. The fire spread and destroyed the warehouse and the goods of other tenants, causing about $400,000 in losses. No one was injured. Investigators identified the defendant from the warehouse's entry logs. According to the state fire marshal, when a building fire is caused by a person's conduct, investigators identify the responsible person in about 1 out of every 2 cases. The defendant has no prior criminal record. A standard risk assessment rates the defendant's likelihood of reoffending as low. The defendant has been convicted, and the court has accepted the facts above.

The defendant owns a small apartment building. Last year the defendant had a heated dispute with one of the tenants over a rent increase. In March, carbon monoxide leaked from the furnace into that tenant's apartment. The defendant deliberately disconnected the furnace's exhaust vent, intending to make the tenant ill. The tenant and the tenant's roommate were hospitalized with carbon monoxide poisoning. Both fully recovered after a week. A fire department inspection after the incident identified the cause and the defendant's role. According to state housing authorities, when carbon monoxide poisoning in rental housing is caused by a landlord's conduct, the responsible landlord is identified in about 1 out of every 2 cases. The defendant has no prior criminal record. A standard risk assessment rates the defendant's likelihood of reoffending as low. The defendant has been convicted, and the court has accepted the facts above.

The defendant owns a restaurant that also caters events. Last year the defendant had a heated dispute with a regular catering client over a cancelled contract. In March, the defendant's restaurant catered a dinner for that client's company. The defendant deliberately mixed spoiled chicken into the meal, intending to make the guests ill. Twelve guests were hospitalized with food poisoning. All fully recovered within a week. Several guests reported their illness to the health department, which traced it to the dinner and to the defendant. According to the state health department, when a food poisoning outbreak is caused by a restaurant's conduct, the responsible business is identified in about 1 out of every 2 cases. The defendant has no prior criminal record. A standard risk assessment rates the defendant's likelihood of reoffending as low. The defendant has been convicted, and the court has accepted the facts above.

The defendant is a contract systems administrator for a regional shipping company. Last year the defendant had a heated dispute with the company's manager over an unpaid invoice. In March, the company's customer and order records were erased from its main server. The defendant deliberately ran a command to erase the records, intending to destroy them. The records could not be recovered. Rebuilding them and the resulting lost business cost the company about $400,000. Server logs identified the defendant's account. According to state cybercrime investigators, when data destruction at a business is caused by an insider's conduct, the responsible person is identified in about 1 out of every 2 cases. The defendant has no prior criminal record. A standard risk assessment rates the defendant's likelihood of reoffending as low. The defendant has been convicted, and the court has accepted the facts above.
